milestone.title: mp-flow skill table-vs-stages drift — extend mp_flow_lint to assert SKILL.md role-binding row matches stages.toml

intent.outcome: make mp-flow-lint enforces that the role-binding table at templates/skills/mp-flow/SKILL.md stays in lockstep with templates/skills/mp-flow/stages.toml — both stage names and role bindings — so a rename in one cannot silently drift the other.

problem.description: scripts/mp_flow_lint.py (95 lines) only checks that SKILL.md has a `## <name>` section per [[stages]] entry in templates/skills/mp-flow/stages.toml. The role-binding table at templates/skills/mp-flow/SKILL.md:13-28 is never checked, and 7 of its 12 Name cells drift from stages.toml: the manifest says Draft / Groom / Specify / Approve / Complete / Remediate / Hand off where the table says Define outcome / Interview & shape / Write acceptance / Approve spec / Mark complete / Remediate findings / Hand-off. stages.toml's own header says the table mirrors the manifest and 'the lint fails' on divergence — today it passes falsely. The canonical data is [[stages]].number / .name / .role, with [role_binding.<role>].stages listing stage numbers per role.

in_scope: Extend scripts/mp_flow_lint.py to parse the SKILL.md role-binding table and assert, per row, that Stage == [[stages]].number, Name == [[stages]].name, and Owner == [[stages]].role; also assert [role_binding.<role>].stages agrees with the per-stage roles. Each mismatch prints one diagnostic naming the stage number, the field, and expected vs actual.
Add a `--skill <path>` / `--manifest <path>` override so the lint can be pointed at fixture files, and a `--json` flag that prints the parsed rows.
Update the SKILL.md role-binding table to the canonical stages.toml names.

Add tests/fixtures/mp-flow-lint/{good,drifted}/ fixtures and a Rust integration test crates/mp/tests/mp_flow_lint_drift.rs that runs the lint against both (good exits 0; drifted exits non-zero with the per-row diagnostic).
Document the table contract in docs/skills/README.md.
out_of_scope: Adding new stages or new roles.
Changing role ownership rules (this is a name-drift fix, not a process change).
Syncing the installed harness copies of the skill (~/.cursor/skills etc.) — `make install` owns that.

acceptance_criteria.description: scripts/mp_flow_lint.py checks every row of the SKILL.md role-binding table (Stage, Name, Owner) against stages.toml and names the stage, field, and expected vs actual on mismatch; --json prints the 12 parsed rows.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: herdr-orc cycle 1: runner commits f0bcdae (S1), 980b2d9 (S1.1), 3b55dd6 (S2), 05e7e4a (S1.1.1); reviewer verdict ok with 5 low findings, commit b97a26a. Orchestrator R5 re-ran all 4 ACs independently and additionally probed the lint with 4 adversarial mutations (Name drift, Owner drift, missing row, renumbering), all correctly exit 1. Reviewer ran 8 probes including duplicate rows and bidirectional role_binding breaks. stages.toml untouched. MP_VERIFY_ALLOW_SHELL=1 required because AC-04 is a shell one-liner (make lint && make consumer-surface-lint); every command was reviewed and executed before opting in.
